title: 1976 AHSME Problem 25
statement: For a sequence \(u_1,\) \(u_2,\) \(\ldots,\) define \(\Delta^1(u_n)=u_{n+1}-u_n\) and, for all integers \(k\gt1,\) \(\Delta^k(u_n)=\Delta^1(\Delta^{k-1}(u_n)).\) If \(u_n=n^3+n,\) then \(\Delta^k(u_n)=0\) for all \(n\)

solutions.text:
Directly, \[ \begin{aligned} \Delta u_n&=3n^2+3n+2,\\ \Delta^2u_n&=6n+6,\\ \Delta^3u_n&=6,\\ \Delta^4u_n&=0. \end{aligned} \] Thus the fourth differences vanish for all \(n,\) but the third differences do not.

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Each forward difference lowers the degree of a polynomial sequence by one
Compute through the constant third difference to see when zero first appears
